title: Professional email
examples: How long should a professional email be?
What makes a subject line effective?
Can I ask for a favour in an email?

explain.say: A good subject line tells the reader what the email is about.
A vague subject line might make your email get ignored.
When making a request, always state it clearly and directly.
Instead of rambling, try to get to your main point quickly.

draw.text: Be Concise: Get to the point

explain.say: In a real job setting, always check the recipient's name first.
A common mistake is burying the request deep in paragraphs.

faq.q: Should I use exclamation marks in professional emails?
faq.a: It is best to use them very sparingly, if at all. Overuse can sound overly emotional or unprofessional. You might also ask, 'Are exclamation marks okay?' or 'How many exclamation points are too many?'
asks: Is it okay to sound excited?
What is the tone of an email?

faq.q: If the request is complex, should I use an attachment?
faq.a: Yes, use an attachment for large documents or detailed data. In the email body, just refer to the attachment clearly. You could also ask, 'Should I send a PDF?' or 'Is an attachment better than text?'
asks: How do I reference a document?

faq.q: What if I need information from multiple people?
faq.a: Use the 'Cc' and 'Bcc' fields correctly. Keep the main request focused so everyone knows their part. You could also ask, 'Who should I copy?' or 'How do I loop in others?'

faq.q: Does the subject line need to include my name?
faq.a: It is usually unnecessary unless you are emailing a large group unfamiliar with you. Keep it focused on the topic itself. You might ask, 'Do I need to sign my name in the subject?' or 'Is my name needed there?'
asks: Is my name required in the subject?
What if I am new to the company?

faq.q: How do I follow up if I do not get a reply?
faq.a: Wait a reasonable amount of time first, perhaps two to three business days. When following up, reference the original email gently. You could also ask, 'How long should I wait?' or 'What is a polite follow-up?'
asks: When is it too soon to follow up?

facts: A strong subject line helps recipients prioritize emails.
Concise requests are best delivered in a single, clear paragraph.
Always proofread for tone and grammar before hitting send.
Use bullet points for lists of required actions.

quiz.say: If you need a colleague to review a document by Friday, where should you place that request?

options.show: In a clear, actionable bullet point near the end.
options.say: In a clear, actionable bullet point near the end.

quiz.why: Placing it clearly ensures the reader does not overlook the required action.

wrong.1: It can sound demanding if not softened with context.
wrong.2: This makes the request easily missed when skimming the email.
wrong.3: The subject line should summarize, not contain the full action item.

quiz.say: A request to reschedule a call should be phrased as:

options.show: I cannot make our meeting time.
options.say: I cannot make our meeting time.

options.show: When are you free next week?
options.say: When are you free next week?

options.show: Could we reschedule our call to Tuesday afternoon?
options.say: Could we reschedule our call to Tuesday afternoon?

quiz.why: This phrasing is polite, proposes a solution, and is easy to answer.

wrong.0: This sounds abrupt and does not offer alternatives.
wrong.1: This puts too much planning work on the recipient.
wrong.2: This is too brief and lacks the necessary polite framing.
